name: Bicycle Health
one_liner: Online Suboxone treatment for opioid use disorder: video visits with a prescriber, coaching and support groups, in 27 states.
best_for: Adults with opioid use disorder who want to start buprenorphine (Suboxone) quickly by video
People with commercial insurance, Medicaid or Medicare in one of Bicycle's 27 states
People who want discreet treatment without visiting a clinic
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who want treatment for alcohol or other drugs only
People who need medically supervised detox or residential care
short_description: Telehealth buprenorphine (Suboxone) treatment for opioid use disorder in 27 states; insurance, Medicaid and Medicare accepted, or $249/month self-pay.
long_description: Bicycle Health is a US telehealth practice that treats opioid use disorder with buprenorphine (Suboxone). Clinicians see you by video, can often send a prescription the same day, and follow up with regular visits; the program also includes lab tests, coaching and support groups. The company says it operates in 27 states and accepts most major commercial plans, Medicaid and Medicare, with most insured patients paying under $35 a month; a directory listing notes Medicaid places are sometimes limited. Self-pay is $249 a month including labs, with the medication billed separately by the pharmacy (roughly $0–$150 depending on coverage). Bicycle Health staff published a descriptive study in BMJ Innovations (2022) reporting that 80% of insured patients were still in treatment at 90 days; there is no randomized trial. Its website privacy policy allows sharing personal information for targeted advertising, though it says it does not sell health information.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (most pay under $35/month); $249/month self-pay
pricing.notes: Self-pay $249/month includes lab tests (previously $199). Suboxone is billed separately by the pharmacy, generally $0–$150 depending on coverage. Most major commercial plans, Medicaid and Medicare accepted; Medicaid capacity can be limited.

privacy.notes: Website policy allows sharing personal information with third parties for marketing and targeted advertising (with an opt-out); says it will not sell or use health information from its secure platform for advertising; clinical records under its HIPAA notice.

faqs.q: How much does Bicycle Health cost?
faqs.a: With insurance, copays typically range from $0-50 per visit. Without insurance, medication management is approximately $195/month. Medication costs (Suboxone) are separate and vary by pharmacy. Many patients qualify for insurance or assistance programs.

faqs.q: Is Bicycle Health legitimate for Suboxone treatment?
faqs.a: Yes, Bicycle Health uses licensed physicians who can legally prescribe buprenorphine for opioid use disorder. The platform follows DEA and state regulations for controlled substance prescribing via telemedicine. An 87% retention rate demonstrates treatment effectiveness.

faqs.q: What states does Bicycle Health operate in?
faqs.a: Bicycle Health operates in 32+ states. Coverage expands regularly. Check their website for current availability in your state. Some states have restrictions on controlled substance telemedicine prescribing.

faqs.q: What support does Bicycle Health include beyond medication?
faqs.a: Beyond prescribing, Bicycle Health provides peer recovery support, therapy access, 24/7 crisis support, and care coordination. The comprehensive approach addresses addiction as a medical condition requiring ongoing support.

patient_summary: You book a video visit with a Bicycle Health clinician, who can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone), often the same day, and you keep regular check-ins plus optional coaching and support groups. Most insured patients pay under $35 a month; self-pay is $249 a month with lab tests included. The medication itself is billed by your pharmacy.
